title: Live Broadcast
description: The whole point of the tracking WebSocket is that a connected customer sees their shipment move without refreshing the page. Prove a real end-to-end round trip: open a socket, trigger an advance through the REST API, and watch the update arrive over the wire.
successCondition: As a customer, book a shipment and open a WebSocket connection to /api/tracking/ws?token=<their accessToken>, confirming the initial { "type": "connected" } message. As a dispatcher/admin (a separate REST call), POST /api/tracking/:id/advance for that customer's shipment. Within a few seconds, the customer's open WebSocket receives a message with type "tracking-update" whose shipment.id matches the advanced shipment and whose shipment.status/currentPosition reflects the new state returned by the advance call.
hints: Keep the WebSocket connection open in one execution context while making the advance REST call from another — this is inherently a two-actor, two-channel test.
Compare the WebSocket message's shipment object field-by-field against the advance endpoint's own HTTP response body — they should describe the identical post-advance state.
